prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE landscape contact sheet showing six successive viewport wireframes for a single vertically scrolling Services webpage for 2 Loons Pickup. Exactly six distinct wide rectangular frames in an even 3 columns by 2 rows, reading left to right then down. Keep all six edges and margins inside image. Thin dark frame edges, clean ivory board, gutters that clearly separate screens. No device hardware or browser chrome. These are wireframes with finished illustrations: large readable headings and illustrated blocks, no filler body copy, only a few specific UI labels. Accurate alignment, crisp pro website layout, deliberate breathing room. Strong visual continuity with the existing site: reference 1 is the live-site style, forest green #19271f, cream #fbf2df, amber #f3bf6a with rust #8f3428 accents, heavy condensed Barlow-style headings and clean DM Sans-like captions, flat squared controls, subtly textured vintage workwear screenprint illustrations. References 2 and 3 are character identity only, preserve faces and outfits: Devin is slim with tousled brown hair, round glasses, dark green jacket. Jonathan has wavy dark hair, subtle mustache/beard and a brick red work shirt. Draw the same two grown men in active work poses throughout. 

Frame 1 "SERVICES". Branded forest green hero, small 2LoonsPickup.com in top bar, strong headline and amber "Request a quote" control on the left, on the right a single large angled print of the two named crew avatars next to their truck. 
Frame 2 "FURNITURE CARRYOUTS". Warm cream background, big half-width image on the left of Devin and Jonathan moving a mustard couch through an open doorway, right-side caption card "Couches, chairs, dressers". 
Frame 3 "STAIRS & HEAVY ITEMS". The standout cinematic frame. Jonathan in his red shirt is the larger foreground character, helping carry a white washing machine UP an interior stairway with visible appliance carrying straps. Devin in green with round glasses is clearly the second worker uphill helping guide and share the load. Show two people working together, a believable appliance and room on the stairs, no tutorial arrows or diagram. Cream callout card in a clear area beside the picture reads "Ask about heavy items" and "Tell us about stairs". 
Frame 4 "OTHER JOBS". Cream editorial collage of exactly three small action print panels, using the same crew: Devin clearing a garage corner, Jonathan moving boxed clutter, both rolling items from the curb to a truck. Under each image a simple legible caption, respectively "Garage corners", "Boxed clutter", "Curbside loads". 
Frame 5 "PICKUP DAY". Amber with dark ink. Crew arriving at a home and talking to a customer at the doorway, silhouetted tree and truck behind them, unobstructed route. One cream caption card with "Before we arrive" and "When we get there". 
Frame 6 "FAQS". Cream/pine closing screen with three horizontal accordion rows reading "Can you take this?", "Should I help carry?", "Who will show up?" and the amber button "Request a quote". Small friendly cropped appearance of both avatars along right edge, secondary to question list.

No extra frame titles or numeric labels outside the mockups. No pricing, guarantees, reviews, claims of availability, competitor logos or slogans. No gloves tutorial or straps tutorial. Prioritize the visual identity and clean hierarchy, clean printed captions with the exact text only. This is a user-review storyboard for a local service site, one coherent page in six stacked sections.
